messages:
devin.k: Heads-up — since ~02:10 UTC we're getting a flurry of short ECC/Xid blips in us-west-2 on gpu-pool-3. Alert manager auto-drained 3 nodes but the cards recovered within a minute each. This churn is killing capacity and backfills.

olga.sre: ugh. Do you have the alert firings? screenshots or timestamps?

devin.k: attaching the alert spikes (copied from alert history): `gpu_ecc_error_count` alerts fired at 02:12, 02:14, 02:19 for cards 0/2/5 on node ids n-07*, all cleared within ~60s.

mike.infra: sounds like noisy samples from DCGM exporter + sampling jitter. Our current rule uses `increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[1m]) > 0` with `for: 0m` which is way too sensitive for brief pulses.

priya.runtime: yep — we see short-lived kernel reports after CUDA context resets that increment counters transiently. We should avoid draining on one sample.

devin.k: proposal: add hysteresis & a "stable-fail" detection. Only mark for drain if errors persist across multiple windows or across multiple metrics (ECC + Xid). Also consider a short mute in alertmanager for repeat <1min salthreads to avoid double-notify.

olga.sre: agreed. What concrete rule changes?

mike.infra: suggestion: use a 10m window and rate-based threshold + count of distinct error events. Example:

```yaml
- alert: GPU_ECC_PersistentErrors
  expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[10m]) >= 3
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "Persistent ECC errors on {{ $labels.gpu_card }}"
```

mike.infra: plus a secondary alert that triggers earlier for ops-visibility (warning) but doesn't auto-drain: `increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[10m]) > 0` with `for: 5m` and severity=warning.

priya.runtime: also propose combining Xid and ECC: `increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[10m])` and require either both or repeat across windows. Eg: mark drain if `(increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[30m]) >= 2) or (increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[30m]) >= 2)`

olga.sre: nice. We should also ensure exporter sample rate isn't spiking due to scrape hiccups — otherwise increases look worse. Can we add a recording rule to smooth the metric? e.g., `gpu_ecc_in_10m = increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[10m])` so alerts reference the recording value.

mike.infra: yep — that keeps expressions simpler and faster. Also add a label `observed_window=10m` so it's obvious in dashboards.

devin.k: action items: (1) mike to draft PR with new recording + two alert rules (warning + persistent critical) and update alertmanager route to not auto-silence warning; (2) priya to update runtime to emit a stable metric `dcgm_exporter_up_latency` so we can correlate; (3) olga to coordinate a small canary rollout in us-west-2 for the rule changes.

priya.runtime: will add the exporter latency metric and a runbook note about not draining on single-sample ECC.

olga.sre: can we also temporarily disable auto-drain policy for gpu-pool-3 until rules are adjusted? That'll avoid upcoming churn.

mike.infra: i can flip the pool policy to manual-drain for that pool for the next 24h. doing that now. will note in cluster-ops channel.

sre-bot: [deploy-notify] Marker: manual-drain-mode enabled for `gpu-pool-3` by mike.infra at 2026-11-03T02:30:45Z

devin.k: thanks. Once PR is up @mike.infra drop the link here and i'll run a short sim with synthetic increments to confirm we don't double-drain.

mike.infra: PR: https://git.redwood/company/infra/merge/1234 (draft) — includes recording rule + warning/critical alert templates + alertmanager route tweak.

olga.sre: I'll schedule a 30m post-change observation window after rollout. If noise persists we escalate to hardware replacement for any card that shows repeated criticals across 3+ windows.

devin.k: sounds good. thanks team :thumbsup:

priya.runtime: follow-up: snippet for the recording rule I'll add to the PR:```yaml
- record: gpu:ecc_in_10m:increase
  expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[10m])
```

mike.infra: perfect. I'll add dashboards panels for `gpu:ecc_in_10m:increase` and `dcgm_xid_in_10m:increase` so SRE can eyeball trends.

olga.sre: copying final plan to the incident playbook and closing this thread once change is live.

devin.k: closing — ping me if any weirdness after the canary.
